content.what_it_is: MATLAB nesting tool that generates the station list station_NC_RI_FL.txt consumed by coupling_file_multi_blocks.m. Places stations at 1-arcminute spacing dx=60.0/3600.0 degrees (L3) along the four boundaries of three nested-grid bounding boxes: NC block lon -79.1..-76.7, lat 33.5..34.746666666666670 (L8-L14); RI block lon -74.5..-69.5, lat 40.25..42.24666666666667 (L68-L74, comment 'actually y(end)=42.233333' L71); FL block lon -81.0..-79.0, lat 24.0..26.75 (L127-L133). For each block, four loops append rows (lat, lon, side_id) to sta: east side at x(end) (L19-L24, L78-L83, L137-L142), west at x(1) (L28-L33, L87-L92, L146-L151), south at y(1) (L37-L42, L96-L101, L155-L160), north at y(end) (L46-L51, L105-L110, L164-L169); id_count increments per side (L17, L26, L35, L44 and analogues) so sides get global IDs 1-4 (NC), 5-8 (RI), 9-12 (FL), matching the side+(kk-1)*4 encoding in the coupling scripts. Sanity checks compare per-block station counts to 2*length(x)+2*length(y) (L53, L112, L171). Each block's outline is plotted and saved as plots/NestBC_NC.jpg (L55-L61), plots/NestBC_RI.jpg (L115-L121), plots/NestBC_FL.jpg (L174-L180). Finally writes all rows in '%f %f %d' format to station_NC_RI_FL.txt (L183-L185).
entities: dx station spacing in degrees L3
x1, x2, y1, y2 block bounds L8-L11, L68-L71, L127-L130

icount_last block boundary marker L63, L124

calls: length L19, L28, L37, L46, L53, L58 and per-block analogues L78-L177
unresolved: sta columns are (lat, lon, side_id) — column 1 is latitude, column 2 longitude (L21-L22); consumers must know this order, and the coupling scripts read only column 3

corner points are duplicated between adjacent sides (east/west loops span all y including y(1) and y(end) which also appear in south/north loops); whether the FUNWAVE STATIONS output expects deduplicated corners is not determinable here
the comment '% 60 times' (L3) does not explain that dx=1/60 degree = 1 arcminute; RI y2 comment (L71) admits the range end is not hit exactly
the NC block plot (L57) plots all rows accumulated so far, correct only because NC is first; RI/FL plots slice by icount_last
